question: In 1934, New York children whose tonsils doctors had judged fine were sent to new doctors. What share did these recommend removing?
answer: Nearly half. Of 389 eleven-year-olds still with tonsils, the first doctors picked 45% for surgery. The rest went to fresh doctors, who picked 46% of them; a third round picked 44% of what was left. Each group of examiners found about the same share to cut, whichever children stood in front of them.
move: When every judge finds the same share guilty, the share belongs to the judges.
ask: When an expert tells me I need something, how would I know if they say it to nearly everyone?
trap: Almost none, since those children had already been examined and cleared.
reference: Bakwin, Pseudodoxia pediatrica, New England Journal of Medicine, 1945
